children.text: Ajitasenavyākaraṇam
children.translated_text: <s>Ajitasenavyākaraṇam</s> (The Prophecy of Ajitasena)

body.text: // om namaḥ sarvajñāya //
body.translated_text: // Oṃ, homage to the All-Knowing One! //

body.text: evaṃ mayā śrutamekasmin samaye bhagavān śrāvastyāṃ viharati sma jetavane anāthapiṇḍadasyārāme mahātā bhikṣusaṅghena sārdhamardhatrayodaśabhirbhikṣusahasraiḥ / tadyathā āyuṣmatā cājñātakauṇḍinyena āyuṣmatā ca mahānāmnā āyuṣmatā ca revatena āyuṣmatā ca vakkulena āyuṣmatā ca śāriputreṇa āyuṣmatā ca pūrṇena maitrāyaṇīputreṇa ca śrāvakaniyutaiḥ / te sarve yena bhagavān yena ca jetavanaṃ vihāraṃ tenopasaṅkrāntā bhagavataḥ pādau śirasābhivandya bhagavataḥ puratastasthurdvātriṃśatā bodhisattvasahasraiḥ / tadyathā sahacittotpādadharmacakrapravartanena ca bodhisattvena mahāsattvena anikṣiptadhureṇa ca bodhisattvena mahāsattvena maitreyeṇa ca bodhisattvena mahāsattvena avalokiteśvareṇa ca bodhisattvena mahāsattvena mahāsthāmaprāptena ca bodhisattvena mahāsattvena / evampramukhairdātriṃśatā bodhisattvasahasraiḥ / te sarve yena bhagavān yena ca jetavanaṃ vihāraṃ tenopasaṅkrāntā bhagavataḥ pādau śirasābhivandya bhagavataḥ puratastasthuḥ / atha khalu bhagavān pūrvāhṇakālasamaye nivāsya pātracīvaramātraḥ śrāvastīṃ mahānagarīṃ piṇḍāya prāviśat / atha bhagavānāyuṣmantamānandamāmantrayate (

children.text: Asv 104
children.translated_text: Asv 104

children.text: ) sma / gacchānanda pātraṃ cakrikaṃ śikyamānaya / athāyuṣmānānando bhagavataḥ śrutamātreṇa pātraṃ cakrikaṃ śikyaṃ bhagavate upanāmayāmāsa / athāyuṣmānānando bhagavataḥ kṛtāñjalipuṭo bhagavantaṃ gāthābhiradhyabhāṣata /
children.translated_text: 'Go, <s>Ānanda</s>, bring the bowl, the wheel-device, and the carrying-net.' Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, upon merely hearing the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s words, offered the bowl, wheel-device, and carrying-net to the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, with palms joined, addressed the <s>Bhagavān</s> in verses:

body.translated_text: Thus have I heard. At one time the <s>Bhagavān</s> was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s> in <s>Jetavana</s>, the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>, together with a great assembly of monks — twelve-and-a-half thousand monks. Namely: with the venerable <s>Ājñātakauṇḍinya</s>, the venerable <s>Mahānāma</s>, the venerable <s>Revata</s>, the venerable <s>Vakkula</s>, the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, the venerable <s>Pūrṇa Maitrāyaṇīputra</s>, and <s>niyutas</s> (myriads) of <s>śrāvakas</s> (hearers). They all approached the <s>Bhagavān</s> and the <s>Jetavana</s> monastery, bowed their heads at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, and stood before the <s>Bhagavān</s> — together with thirty-two thousand <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. Namely: the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Sahacittotpādadharmacakrapravartana</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Anikṣiptadhura</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Maitreya</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Mahāsthāmaprāpta</s> — led by these, thirty-two thousand <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. They all approached the <s>Bhagavān</s> and the <s>Jetavana</s> monastery, bowed their heads at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, and stood before the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, in the forenoon, having dressed and taking only his bowl and robe, entered the great city of <s>Śrāvastī</s> for alms. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>:

children.text: yadā tvaṃ praviśasi piṇḍapātika vimocaye tvaṃ bahavaṃ hi prāṇinām /
children.translated_text: When you enter for alms, O one who goes for alms-food, you liberate many living beings;

children.text: uttāraye tvaṃ bahavaṃ hi sattvā narakabhayājjātijarāmahābhayā //
children.translated_text: you rescue many beings from the great fear of hell, birth, old age, and terrible danger.

children.text: saṃsāraduḥkhakalilā mahābhayādvimocaye tvaṃ nara lokanāyaka /
children.translated_text: From the great fear of suffering in <s>saṃsāra</s> (the cycle of existence), you liberate people, O World-Leader;

children.text: mahānubhāvo varadakṣiṇīyo vimocayitvā punaraṃ hi āgamī //
children.translated_text: of great power, worthy of the best offerings, having liberated them, you return again.

body.text: athāyuṣmānānando bhagavata imā gāthā bhāṣitvā tūṣṇīṃ sthito 'bhūt / atha bhagavān śrāvastyāṃ mahānagaryāṃ nātidūre sthito 'bhūt / atha te sarve gavākṣatoraṇaniryūhakā hiraṇyamayāḥ sphaṭikamayā rūpyamayāḥ prādurabhūvan / tathā śrāvastyāṃ mahānagaryāṃ mahāntaṃ janakāyaṃ saṃsthito 'bhūvan / atha sa janakāyaḥ saṃśayajāto babhūva ko hetuḥ kaḥ pratyayaḥ nagarasya śubhanimittaṃ prādurabhūt / mā cedaṃ nagaraṃ bhasmapralayaṃ syāt / atha tatra janakāye anekavarṣaśatasahasrakoṭīko (

children.text: Asv 105
children.translated_text: Asv 105

children.text: ) vṛddhamahallakaḥ puruṣaḥ saṃsthito 'bhūt / atha sa puruṣastaṃ janakāyaṃ samāśvāsayannevamāha / mā bhaiṣurbhoḥ kulaputrāḥ / asminneva pṛthivīpradeśe jetavanaṃ nāma vihāraḥ / tatra śākyamunirnāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksambuddho vidyācaraṇasampannaḥ sugato lokavidanuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca buddho bhagavān / so 'yaṃ śrāvastīṃ mahānagarīṃ piṇḍāya prāviśat / tasyāgamanakālasamaye idaṃ śubhanimittamabhūt / atha sa janakāyastaṃ jīrṇakaṃ puruṣaṃ kṛtāñjalirevamāha / yattasya bhagavatastathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksambuddhasya guṇavarṇasamudīraṇasamaye idaṃ śubhanimittamabhūt / dṛṣṭamātrasya tasya tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksambuddhasya kīdṛśaḥ puṇyābhisaṃskāro bhaviṣyati / atha sa jīrṇakapuruṣastaṃ janakāyaṃ bhagavato guṇavarṇasamudīraṇatayā gāthābhiradhyabhāṣata /
children.translated_text: ) an aged, very old man, many hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of years old. That man reassured the crowd, saying: 'Do not fear, O sons of good family! In this very region of the earth there is a monastery called <s>Jetavana</s>. There dwells the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One named <s>Śākyamuni</s> — endowed with knowledge and conduct, the <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One), knower of the world, unsurpassed, tamer of those to be tamed, teacher of gods and men, the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>. He has entered the great city of <s>Śrāvastī</s> for alms. At the time of his arrival, this auspicious sign appeared.' Then that crowd, with palms joined, addressed the old man thus: 'Since this auspicious sign appeared at the time of proclaiming the virtues and praises of that <s>Bhagavān</s>, that <s>Tathāgata</s>, that <s>Arhat</s>, that Perfectly Awakened One — how great must be the accumulation of merit from merely seeing that <s>Tathāgata</s>, that <s>Arhat</s>, that Perfectly Awakened One!' Then that old man, by way of proclaiming the virtues and praises of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, addressed the crowd in verses:

body.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, having spoken these verses to the <s>Bhagavān</s>, stood silently. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> stood not far from the great city of <s>Śrāvastī</s>. And all those windows, gateways, and balconies appeared made of gold, crystal, and silver. And in the great city of <s>Śrāvastī</s>, a great crowd of people had assembled. That crowd became filled with doubt: 'What is the cause? What is the condition? An auspicious sign has appeared in the city. Or could this city be about to be reduced to ashes?' And among that crowd, there stood (

children.text: yo lokanāthasya hi nāmu yaḥ śruṇe saṃsāraduḥkhā vinimuktu so naro /
children.translated_text: Whoever hears the name of the Protector of the World — that person is freed from the suffering of <s>saṃsāra</s>;

children.text: āpāyagāmī na kadāci bheṣyate svargaṃ ca so yāsyati śīghramevam //
children.translated_text: he will never go to the lower realms of existence, and he will quickly proceed to heaven in this way.

body.text:
yo lokanāthasya hi nāmu yaḥ śruṇe dṛḍhapratijño bahukalpakoṭibhiḥ /
mahānubhāvo sugato mahātmanaḥ kalpānakoṭīnayutānacintiyān // (

children.text: Asv 106
children.translated_text: Asv 106

children.text: so bodhisattvo sthita gaṅgavālukān kadāci so gacchati durgatī bhayam /
children.translated_text: that <s>Bodhisattva</s>, standing firm as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, will never go to the fearful lower realms;

children.text: yo lokanāthasya hi nāmu yaḥ śruṇe āpāyagāmī na kadāci bheṣyate //
children.translated_text: whoever hears the name of the Protector of the World will never go to the lower realms of existence.

body.translated_text: Whoever hears the name of the Protector of the World — of firm resolve, through many <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s> (eons), of great power, the <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One), the great soul, through inconceivable <s>niyutas</s> of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s> — (

children.text: kalpānakoṭīnayutānacintiyā rājā sa bhotī sada cakravartī /
children.translated_text: Through inconceivable <s>niyutas</s> of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, he will always be a king, a <s>Cakravartin</s> (universal monarch);

children.text: yo lokanāthasya hi nāmu dhārayet //
children.translated_text: whoever upholds the name of the Protector of the World.

children.text: yat kiñci pūrvaṃ sada pāpu yat kṛtaṃ sarvaṃ kṣayaṃ yāsyati śīghrametat /
children.translated_text: Whatever sin was formerly committed — all of it will quickly go to destruction;

children.text: śakropi devendramahānubhāvo kalpānakoṭīnayutānacintiyā //
children.translated_text: <s>Śakra</s> too, lord of the gods, of great power, through inconceivable <s>niyutas</s> of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>.

children.text: sukhāvatīṃ gacchati buddhakṣetraṃ paryaṅkabaddho sa ca bodhisattvo /
children.translated_text: He goes to <s>Sukhāvatī</s> (the Land of Bliss), the <s>Buddha</s>-field, that <s>Bodhisattva</s>, seated cross-legged;

children.text: brahmasvaro susvaru mañjughoṣa bhavanti varṣānasahasrakoṭibhiḥ //
children.translated_text: of <s>Brahma</s>-voice, of beautiful voice, of sweet sound — for <s>koṭis</s> of thousands of years they will be such.

body.text: apāyagāmī na kadāci bheṣyate yo lokanāthasya hi nāmu dhārayet /
body.translated_text: He will never go to the lower realms of existence, whoever upholds the name of the Protector of the World.

body.text: atha sa jīrṇakaḥ purūṣo janakāyaṃ bhagavato guṇavarṇamudīrayitvā tūṣṇīṃ sthito 'bhūt / atha bhagavān pūrveṇa nagaradvāreṇa śrāvastīṃ mahānagarīṃ praviṣṭo 'bhut / tatra ca nagaradvāre dvādaśakoṭyaḥ padmānāṃ prādurabhūvan / teṣu ca padmeṣu dvādaśakoṭyo bodhisattvānāṃ paryaṅkaniṣaṇṇāḥ (

children.text: Asv 107
children.translated_text: Asv 107

children.text: ) prādurabhūvan prāñjalayaḥ / atha bhagavataḥ praviṣṭamātreṇa śrāvastyāṃ mahānagaryāṃ navanavatikoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇi sattvānāṃ sukhāvatyāṃ lokadhātau pratiṣṭhāpitāni caturaśītisattvakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇyābhiratyā lokadhātorakṣobhyatathāgatasya buddhakṣetre pratiṣṭhāpitāni /
children.translated_text: ), appeared with palms joined. Upon the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s mere entry into the great city of <s>Śrāvastī</s>, ninety-nine hundred thousand <s>koṭi-niyutas</s> of beings were established in the world-realm of <s>Sukhāvatī</s> (the Land of Bliss), and eighty-four hundred thousand <s>koṭi-niyutas</s> of beings were established in the <s>Buddha</s>-field of the <s>Tathāgata Akṣobhya</s> in the world-realm of <s>Abhirati</s> (Supreme Delight).

body.translated_text: Then that old man, having proclaimed the virtues and praises of the <s>Bhagavān</s> to the crowd, stood silently. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> entered the great city of <s>Śrāvastī</s> through the eastern gate. And at that city gate, twelve <s>koṭis</s> (ten millions) of lotuses appeared. Upon those lotuses, twelve <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, seated cross-legged (

body.text: atha bhagavān ānandena saha nagaravalambikāyā dārikāya gṛhe samāgato 'bhūta / atha bhagavān nagaravalambikāyā dārikāyā gṛhe cakrikaṃ kaṭakaṭāpayāmāsa / atha sā dārikā taṃ cakrīśabdaṃ śrutvā saṃśayajātābhūt / ko hetuḥ kaḥ pratyayaḥ / mama gṛhe na kadācit piṇḍapātika āgato 'bhūt / atha sa nagaravalambikā dārikā śūnyākāragṛhe niṣaṇṇā aśrukaṇṭhī rudantī paridevantī sthitābhūt tīkṣṇadhāramasiṃ gaveṣantī paridevantī rudantī sthitābhūt / atha sā dārikā śūnyākāragṛhe niṣaṇṇā paridevantī aśrukaṇṭhī rudantī gāthābhiradhyabhāṣata /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, together with <s>Ānanda</s>, arrived at the house of the girl <s>Nagaravalambikā</s>. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> clicked the wheel-device at the house of the girl <s>Nagaravalambikā</s>. That girl, hearing the sound of the wheel-device, became filled with doubt: 'What is the cause? What is the condition? Never before has an alms-seeker come to my house.' Then the girl <s>Nagaravalambikā</s>, sitting in an empty room of the house, her throat choked with tears, weeping and lamenting, stood searching for a sharp-edged sword, lamenting and weeping. Then that girl, sitting in the empty room, lamenting, her throat choked with tears, weeping, spoke in verses:

children.text: aho bata duḥkhu daridrake gṛhe varaṃ mama maraṇu na cāpi jīvitam /
children.translated_text: Alas, how sorrowful in this poor house! Better for me is death than this life;

children.text: kiṃ cāpi me kāryuṣu jīvitena yadyaivāhaṃ duḥkhu śarīra pīḍitam //
children.translated_text: what use is life to me in such circumstances, when I am thus afflicted with suffering in body?

body.text:
kana.......................hyatrāṇaṃ bhavate parāyaṇam /
anāthabhūtā ahamadyameva yadyaivāhaṃ jāta daridrake gṛhe // (

children.text: Asv 108
children.translated_text: Asv 108

body.translated_text: [damaged text]...without refuge, without recourse — I am today without a protector, since I was born in this poor house. (

body.text: atha sa nagaravalambikā dārikā śūnyākāragṛhe niṣaṇṇā imā gāthā bhāṣitvā tūṣṇīṃ sthitābhūt /
body.translated_text: Then the girl <s>Nagaravalambikā</s>, sitting in the empty room, having spoken these verses, stood silently.

body.text: atha śuddhavāsakāyiko devaputro 'ntarīkṣagataḥ sthitaścintayati sma / paśyeccedimāṃ bhagavān / anekaduṣkarakoṭiniyutaśatasahasracīrṇacaritaḥ sa śākyamunistathāgato nagaravalambikāyā dārikāyā gṛhe sthito 'bhūt / atha śuddhavāsakāyiko devaputraḥ śatasahasramūlyaṃ muktāhāraṃ gṛhītvā śatarasabhojanapiṭakaṃ gṛhītvā kāśikāni vastrāṇi gṛhītvā yena nagaravalambikāyā dārikāyā gṛhaṃ tenopasaṅkrānto 'bhūt / atha śuddhavāsakāyiko devaputro nagaravalambikāṃ dārikāmevamāha / prāvara dārike imāni kāśikāni vastrāṇi imānyanekaśatasahasramūlyānyābharaṇāni / prāvṛtya cedaṃ śatasahasramūlyaṃ muktāhāraṃ gṛhītvā imaṃ śatarasabhojanapiṭakaṃ gṛhītvā bhagavantamupanāmaya / atha sā dārikā tāni kāśikāni vastrāṇi prāvṛtya śatasahasramūlyaṃ muktāhāraṃ gṛhītvā taṃ śatarasabhojanapiṭakaṃ gṛhītvā yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṅkrāntā / upasaṅkramya bhagavantamupanāmayati sma / atha bhagavān tāṃ nagaravalambikāmevamāha / pariṇāmaya tvaṃ dārike yathā pariṇāmitaṃ vipaśyiśikhiviśvabhūkkakutasundakanakamunikāśyapaprabhṛtibhiḥ sadbhistathāgatairarhadbhiḥ samyaksambuddhaiḥ / anto bhaviṣyati strībhāvādanto bhaviṣyati daridragṛhāt / atha sā dārikā taṃ piṇḍapātaṃ pariṇāmayitvā (

children.text: Asv 109
children.translated_text: Asv 109

children.text: ) bhagavantamupanāmayāmāsa / anena piṇḍapātakuśalamūlena mā kaśmiṃścid daridragṛhe upapadyeya /
children.translated_text: offered it to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: "By this root of merit from alms-food, may I not be reborn in any poor household."

body.translated_text: Then a god-son of the <s>Śuddhāvāsakāyika</s> (Pure Abodes) class, standing in mid-air, thought: "If only the <s>Bhagavān</s> could see this!" That <s>Śākyamuni Tathāgata</s>, who had practiced through countless hundreds of thousands of millions of difficult deeds, had been standing in the house of the girl <s>Nagaravalambikā</s>. Then the <s>Śuddhāvāsakāyika</s> god-son, having taken a pearl necklace worth a hundred thousand, a basket of food with a hundred flavors, and <s>Kāśika</s> (Benaras) garments, approached the house of the girl <s>Nagaravalambikā</s>. Then the <s>Śuddhāvāsakāyika</s> god-son said to the girl <s>Nagaravalambikā</s>: "Put on these <s>Kāśika</s> garments, girl, and these ornaments worth many hundreds of thousands. Having put them on, take this pearl necklace worth a hundred thousand and this basket of food with a hundred flavors, and offer them to the <s>Bhagavān</s>." Then that girl, having put on those <s>Kāśika</s> garments, having taken the pearl necklace worth a hundred thousand and that basket of food with a hundred flavors, approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Having approached, she offered them to the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> said to that <s>Nagaravalambikā</s>: "Dedicate the merit, girl, just as it was dedicated by <s>Vipaśyin</s>, <s>Śikhin</s>, <s>Viśvabhū</s>, <s>Kakutsunda</s>, <s>Kanakamuni</s>, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, and other true <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>arhats</s>, perfectly enlightened ones. There will be an end to the female state; there will be an end to the poor household." Then that girl, having dedicated the merit of that alms-food,

body.text: atha sā nagaravalambikā dārikā taṃ piṇḍapātaṃ pariṇāmayitvā bhagavate dattvā svagṛhagamanamārabdhā / atha bhagavān tāṃ nagaravalambikāṃ dārikāmevamāha / pratinivartasva dārike / pūrvejātinidānaṃ samanusmarāmi / tadahaṃ parikīrtayiṣyāmi / atha sā dārikā pratinivṛtya sarvāṅgapraṇipātena bhagavantaṃ prapatitā / atha sā nagaravalambikā dārikā bhagavantaṃ gāthābhiradhyabhāṣata /
body.translated_text: Then the girl <s>Nagaravalambikā</s>, having dedicated and given that alms-food to the <s>Bhagavān</s>, began to go to her house. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> said to the girl <s>Nagaravalambikā</s>: "Turn back, girl. I recall the story of a previous birth. I shall relate it." Then that girl, having turned back, prostrated before the <s>Bhagavān</s> with her whole body. Then the girl <s>Nagaravalambikā</s> addressed the <s>Bhagavān</s> with verses:

children.text: avaśyaṃ me pūrvakṛtena karmaṇā yenāhaṃ jāta daridrake gṛhe /
children.translated_text: "Certainly by my previously performed <s>karma</s> I was born in a poor household;

children.text: karohi kāruṇya mamaṃ hi duḥkhita vinivartayasva narakā hi pālān //
children.translated_text: show compassion to me who is suffering, turn me away from the guardians of hell!

children.text: karohi kāruṇya mama duḥkhitāyā istribhāvā upapannu nāyaka /
children.translated_text: Show compassion to me who is suffering, born in the female state, O Leader;

children.text: tvaṃ lokanātha jaravyādhiśoka vimocaye maṃ mama duḥkhitāyāḥ //
children.translated_text: You, O Lord of the World, free me from old age, disease, and sorrow, for I am suffering!

trāṇaṃ bhavāhī śaraṇaṃ parāyaṇaṃ vimocayāhī mama duḥkhitāyāḥ /

children.translated_text: and I shall liberate all from the ocean of suffering. Be my refuge, shelter, and final resort!

body.translated_text: Be my refuge, shelter, and final resort; free me who is suffering! For you, O Lord, have made the vow that whatever beings exist here in <s>Jambudvīpa</s>,

children.text: tvayaṃ hi nātha mayi mocayī jagat avaśyaṃ me pūrvakṛtena karmaṇā /
children.translated_text: You, O Lord, shall liberate me and the world. Certainly by my previously performed <s>karma</s>,

children.text: yenāhaṃ jātu daridrake gṛhe trāṇaṃ bhavāhī mama duḥkhitāyāḥ //
children.translated_text: I was born in a poor household. Be my refuge, for I am suffering!

children.text: bhavaṃ tu nātha jaravyādhimocakaṃ trāṇaṃ bhavāhī guṇa sañcitāgra /
children.translated_text: You, O Lord, are the liberator from old age and disease. Be my refuge, O supreme accumulator of virtues;

children.text: na cā kariṣye punareva pāpaṃ yadvedayāmī imi vedanāni //
children.translated_text: I shall never again commit sin — I experience these painful feelings!

children.text: kṛpaṃ jani...............magra sattvā trāṇaṃ bhavāhī śaraṇaṃ parāyaṇam /
children.translated_text: Having generated compassion... supreme... beings. Be my refuge, shelter, and final resort;

children.translated_text: whatever beings exist here in <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, may they hold the name in the future time!

children.text: parinirvṛtasya tata paścakāle bhaviṣyati śāsanavipralopam /
children.translated_text: After the <s>Parinirvāṇa</s>, in the future time, there will be the decline of the teaching;

children.text: yatakiñci pāpaṃ tadapūrva yat kṛtaṃ sarvaṃ kṣayaṃ yāsyati śīghrametat //
children.translated_text: whatever sin was previously committed, all of that will swiftly reach destruction!"

body.text: atha sā nagaravalambikā dārikā bhagavantaṃ gāthā bhāṣitvā punarapi gṛhagamanamārabdhā / atha bhagavān tāṃ nagaravalambikāṃ (

children.text: parikīrtaya lokavināyakādya yadyat kṛtaṃ pāpa sadā sudāruṇam /

children.translated_text: certainly terrible sin was committed by me, by which I was born in a poor household!

children.text: tvaṃ sārthavāhu iha sarvaloke vimocaye mam iha istribhāvā /
children.translated_text: You are the caravan leader of the entire world — free me from the female state!

children.text: trāṇaṃ bhavāhī śaraṇaṃ parāyaṇaṃ kṛtajñahaṃ nitya bhavāmi nāyake //
children.translated_text: Be my refuge, shelter, and final resort; I shall always be grateful to the Leader!

children.text: saṃśrāvaye mam imu dharmanetrī nāsau kadācittajate apāyam /
children.translated_text: Let me hear this <s>Dharma</s>-eye, by which one is never born in a woeful state;

children.text: saṃśodhayī karma yathākṛtaṃ mayā trāṇaṃ bhavāhī śaraṇaṃ parāyaṇam //
children.translated_text: purify the <s>karma</s> that was performed by me. Be my refuge, shelter, and final resort!

body.text: asaṅgajñānī varalokanāyaka vandāmi nātha śaraṇaṃ kṛtāñjalī //
body.translated_text: O possessor of unattached knowledge, supreme Guide of the World, I salute you, O Lord, my refuge, with joined palms!"

children.text: ) khalu punaḥ samayena padmāvatī nāma rājadhānyabhūt / tena khalu punaḥ samayena padmāvatyāṃ rājadhānyāṃ padmaprabho nāma gṛhapatirabhūt / tasya padmaprabhasya gṛhapatestvaṃ duhitā 'bhūḥ / tena khalu punaḥ samayena grāmanagaranigamajanapadeṣu piṇḍapātiko bhikṣuḥ piṇḍapātāyāvatarati / yadā tvadgṛhamāgato 'bhūta tadā tvaṃ dārike piṇḍapātaṃ gṛhītvā gṛhānniṣkrāntā punareva praviṣṭā 'bhūḥ / na cāhaṃ muṇḍitaśiraso 'dhanyasya piṇḍapātaṃ dāsyāmi / tena karmopacayena tvayā dārike dvādaśakalpasahasrāṇi punaḥ punardaridragṛhe duḥkhānyanubhūtāni / ekena tvayā dārike kuśalamūlena bodhivyākaraṇaṃ pratilapsyase / yattvayā tasya bhikṣo rūpaliṅgasaṃsthā na dṛṣṭā bhaviṣyasi tvaṃ dārike anāgate 'dhvani acintyairaparimāṇaiḥ kalpairnagaradhvajo nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksambuddho vidyācaraṇasampannaḥ sugato lokavidanuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca buddho bhagavān loke / atha sā dārikā bhagavantaṃ triḥ pradakṣiṇaṃ kṛtvaivamāha / kīdṛśaṃ bhagavan mama buddhakṣetraṃ bhaviṣyati yatraivāhaṃ buddho bhaviṣyāmi / bhagavānāha / aparimitaguṇasañcayā nāma sā buddhakṣetraṃ bhaviṣyati / yādṛaśī ca sā sukhāvatī lokadhātuḥ tādṛśaṃ tadbuddhakṣetraṃ bhaviṣyati / paryaṅkaniṣaṇṇā āryopapādukā bodhisattvā bhaviṣyanti / īdṛśaṃ tadbuddhakṣetram / (
children.translated_text: time there was a royal capital called <s>Padmāvatī</s>. At that time in the royal capital <s>Padmāvatī</s> there was a householder named <s>Padmaprabha</s>. You were the daughter of that householder <s>Padmaprabha</s>. At that time, a monk who subsisted on alms went down to villages, cities, market towns, and regions for alms. When he came to your house, you, girl, having taken the alms-food, went out of the house and then came back in again, saying: 'I shall not give alms-food to this shaven-headed, unfortunate one!' By that accumulation of <s>karma</s>, girl, you experienced suffering in poor households again and again for twelve thousand <s>kalpas</s>. By one root of merit, girl, you will obtain the prediction of <s>bodhi</s> (awakening). Since you did not see the form, marks, and figure of that monk, you, girl, in the future, after inconceivable and immeasurable <s>kalpas</s>, will become a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Nagaradhvaja</s>, an <s>arhat</s>, a perfectly enlightened one, perfect in knowledge and conduct, a <s>Sugata</s>, knower of the world, unsurpassed, charioteer of men to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, a <s>Buddha</s>, a <s>Bhagavān</s> in the world." Then that girl, having circumambulated the <s>Bhagavān</s> three times, said: "What will my <s>buddhakṣetra</s> (buddha-field) be like, <s>Bhagavān</s>, where I shall become a <s>Buddha</s>?" The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "That <s>buddhakṣetra</s> will be named <s>Aparimitaguṇasañcayā</s> (Accumulation of Limitless Qualities). Just as the world-realm <s>Sukhāvatī</s> is, so will that <s>buddhakṣetra</s> be. The <s>bodhisattvas</s> will be noble, spontaneously born, seated cross-legged. Such will that <s>buddhakṣetra</s> be.

At that

body.text: atha ca sā dārikā tuṣṭā udagrā āttamanāḥ pramuditā prītisaumanasyajātā svagṛhagamanamārabdhā / atha bhagavāṃstāṃ dārikāmevamāha / tvaṃ dārike saptame divase kālaṃ kariṣyasi / kālaṃ kṛtvā / pūrvasyāndiśi magadhaviṣaye rājā ajitaseno nāma / tasya rājño 'jitasenasya antaḥpurasahasramasti / tasya khalu punā rājño 'jitasenasya putro janiṣyase / eṣa eva tava paścimo garbhavāso bhaviṣyati /
body.translated_text: Then that girl, pleased, elated, joyful, delighted, filled with gladness and satisfaction, began to go to her house. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> said to that girl: "You, girl, will die on the seventh day. After dying, to the east, in the realm of <s>Magadha</s>, there is a king named <s>Ajitasena</s>. That king <s>Ajitasena</s> has a thousand women in his inner quarters. You will be born as the son of that king <s>Ajitasena</s>. This will be your last womb-dwelling."

body.text: atha bhagavān paścimakena nagaradvāreṇa śrāvastyā mahānagaryā niṣkrānto yena jetavanaṃ vihārastenopasaṅkrāntaḥ / athāyuṣmānānando bhagavantaṃ dūrata evāgacchantaṃ dṛṣṭvā pādau śirasābhivandya triḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya bhagavantaṃ gāthābhiradhyabhāṣata /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> departed from the great city of <s>Śrāvastī</s> through the western gate and approached the <s>Jetavana</s> monastery. Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, seeing the <s>Bhagavān</s> coming from afar, saluted his feet with his head, circumambulated him three times, and addressed the <s>Bhagavān</s> with verses:

children.text: suvarṇavarṇaṃ varalakṣaṇārcitaṃ dvāviṃśatilakṣaṇarūpadhāriṇam /
children.translated_text: "Of golden hue, adorned with supreme marks, bearing the form of thirty-two marks,

children.text: yadā tvayā āgatu piṇḍapātikā vimocayitvā iha sarvasattvā //
children.translated_text: when you came on the alms-round, having liberated all beings here,

children.translated_text: you established all beings in happiness; the power of <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness) has been accomplished by you for the entire world;

children.translated_text: that excellent alms-food, O Leader — by it the world has been freed from fear!

body.translated_text: Those <s>bodhisattvas</s> here in <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, all show your path;

children.translated_text: After your <s>Parinirvāṇa</s>, in the future time, there will be the decline of the teaching;

children.text: imaṃ nayaṃ dhārayi sūtraratnam //
children.translated_text: uphold this excellent <s>sūtra</s>, this jewel of the teaching."

body.text: athāyuṣmānānanda imā gāthā bhāṣitvā bhagavantaṃ triḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya bhagavataḥ puratastasthau / atha bhagavānāyuṣmantamānandamāmantrayate sma / gacchānanda gaṇḍīmākoṭaya / te śrāvakāḥ paribhokṣyanti piṇḍapātam / athāyuṣmānānando bhagavantamāmantrayate sma / kīdṛśaṃ bhagavan gaṇḍīśabdasya kuśalamūlaṃ bhaviṣyati / bhagavānāha / śṛṇu ānanda gaṇḍīśabdasya kuśalamūlaṃ parikīrtayāmi / ye kecidānanda gaṇḍīśabdaṃ śroṣyanti teṣāṃ pañcānantaryāṇi kṛtyāni parikṣayaṃ yāsyanti / avaivartikāste bhaviṣyanti kṣipraṃ cānuttarāṃ samyaksambodhimabhisambhotsyante / ānanda āha / kīdṛśaṃ bhagavaṃstaiḥ sattvaiḥ kuśalamūlamavaropim / bhagavānāha / śṛṇu ānanda ye sattvāḥ paścime kāle paścime samaye mama parinirvṛtasya saddharmavipralope vartamāne saddharmasyāntardhānakālasamaye grāmanagaranigamajanapadarāṣṭrarājadhānīṣu ye sattvā vā araṇyāyatane gaṇḍayākoṭanaśabdaṃ śroṣyanti namo buddhāyeti kariṣyanti teṣāṃ pañcānantaryāṇi karmāṇi parikṣayaṃ (

) yāsyanti / īdṛśānyānanda gaṇḍīśabdasya kuśalamūlāni / athāyuṣmānānandaḥ śāntapraśāntena gaṇḍīmākoṭayate sma / atha tena gaṇḍīśabdena sarve te mahāśrāvakāḥ sannipatitā abhūvan / yathā yathā āsane niṣaṇṇāḥ piṇḍapātaṃ paribhuñjante sma / atha tatraiva śrāvakamadhye nandimitro nāma mahāśrāvakaḥ sannipatito 'bhūt sanniṣaṇṇaḥ / atha bhagavānāyuṣmantaṃ nandimitraṃ mahāśrāvakamāmantrayate sma / gaccha tvaṃ nandimitra mahāśrāvaka pūrvasyāndiśi magadhaviṣaye rājño 'jitasenasya kalyāṇamitraparicaryāṃ kuru / atha nandimitro mahāśrāvako bhagavantamevamāha / na bhagavan śakṣyāmastaṃ pṛthivīpradeśaṃ gantum / durāsadāste sattvāḥ / te māṃ jīvitādvyavaropayiṣyanti / atha bhagavānāyuṣmantaṃ taṃ nandimitraṃ mahāśrāvakamevamāha / na te sattvāste śakṣyante bālāgramapi kampayituṃ prāgeva jīvitādvyavaropayitum / atha nandimitro mahāśrāvakaḥ pratyūṣakālasamaye suvarṇavarṇaṃ vastraṃ prāvṛtya yena pūrvasyāndiśi magadhaviṣaye rājño 'jitasenasya rājadhānī tenānukrānto 'bhut / atha rājā ajitasenastaṃ nandimitraṃ mahāśrāvakaṃ dṛṣṭvā tuṣṭa udagra āttamanāḥ pramuditaḥ prītisaumanasyajāto 'bhūt / atha rājñājitasenena amātyaḥ preṣito 'bhūt / gacchainaṃ bhikṣumānaya / tadā so 'mātyo yena nandimitro mahāśrāvakastenopasaṅkrāntaḥ (
children.translated_text: Such, <s>Ānanda</s>, are the wholesome roots of the bell's sound." Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> struck the bell peacefully and calmly. Then, by that sound of the bell, all those great <s>śrāvakas</s> assembled. As they sat down in their seats, they partook of the alms-food. Then, in that very assembly of <s>śrāvakas</s>, a great <s>śrāvaka</s> named <s>Nandimitra</s> assembled and sat down. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the venerable <s>Nandimitra</s>, the great <s>śrāvaka</s>: "Go, <s>Nandimitra</s>, great <s>śrāvaka</s>, to the eastern direction, to the land of <s>Magadha</s>, and serve as a spiritual friend (<s>kalyāṇamitra</s>) to King <s>Ajitasena</s>." Then <s>Nandimitra</s>, the great <s>śrāvaka</s>, said to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: "I am not able, <s>Bhagavān</s>, to go to that region of the earth. Those beings are difficult to approach. They will take my life." Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the venerable <s>Nandimitra</s>, the great <s>śrāvaka</s>, thus: "Those beings will not be able to move even a tip of your hair, let alone take your life." Then <s>Nandimitra</s>, the great <s>śrāvaka</s>, at the break of dawn, wrapping himself in a golden-colored robe, proceeded toward the eastern direction, to the capital of King <s>Ajitasena</s> in the land of <s>Magadha</s>. Then King <s>Ajitasena</s>, upon seeing <s>Nandimitra</s> the great <s>śrāvaka</s>, became pleased, elated, delighted, joyful, and filled with delight and happiness. Then King <s>Ajitasena</s> sent a minister: "Go and bring that monk." Then that minister approached <s>Nandimitra</s> the great <s>śrāvaka</s>.

children.translated_text: Then that minister said to <s>Nandimitra</s> the great <s>śrāvaka</s>: "Come, great <s>śrāvaka</s>, monk, the king commands you." Then <s>Nandimitra</s> the great <s>śrāvaka</s> said to the minister: "What business does the king have with me? What will the king do for me?" Then the minister approached King <s>Ajitasena</s> and said to King <s>Ajitasena</s>: "That monk will not come to your side." Then King <s>Ajitasena</s> sent five hundred ministers. But that monk would not come to the side of King <s>Ajitasena</s>. Then the king himself, in his own person, approached <s>Nandimitra</s> the great <s>śrāvaka</s>. Having approached, with joined palms he said: "Come, O monk, enter my capital city." Then King <s>Ajitasena</s>, taking that monk by the right hand, entered his own capital city. Then King <s>Ajitasena</s> gave a lion-throne to the monk <s>Nandimitra</s>. Then King <s>Ajitasena</s>, sitting on a modest chair, said to <s>Nandimitra</s> the great <s>śrāvaka</s>: "Where are you going, monk? What is the reason? What is the occasion?" Then <s>Nandimitra</s> the great <s>śrāvaka</s> said to King <s>Ajitasena</s>: "All those who have gone forth as monks subsist on alms; they wander about collecting alms-food and eat." Then King <s>Ajitasena</s> said to <s>Nandimitra</s> the great <s>śrāvaka</s>: "Partake of alms-food in my house. I shall provide alms-food for as long as you live. If you, O monk, have need of my own flesh, I shall give my own flesh." Then <s>Nandimitra</s> the great <s>śrāvaka</s> addressed King <s>Ajitasena</s> with verses:

body.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, having spoken these verses, circumambulated the <s>Bhagavān</s> three times and stood before him. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: "Go, <s>Ānanda</s>, and strike the bell. The <s>śrāvakas</s> will partake of the alms-food." Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> addressed the <s>Bhagavān</s>: "What, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, will be the wholesome root of the bell's sound?" The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "Listen, <s>Ānanda</s>, I shall proclaim the wholesome root of the bell's sound. Whoever, <s>Ānanda</s>, shall hear the sound of the bell, their five heinous actions shall be exhausted. They shall become non-retrogressing and shall quickly attain unsurpassed perfect awakening." <s>Ānanda</s> said: "What wholesome root was planted by those beings, O <s>Bhagavān</s>?" The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "Listen, <s>Ānanda</s>. Those beings who, in the final time, in the final period, when I have passed into <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, when the decline of the true <s>Dharma</s> is occurring, at the time of the disappearance of the true <s>Dharma</s>, in villages, towns, market towns, inhabited places, kingdoms, and capital cities—those beings who, even in a forest dwelling, shall hear the sound of the striking of the bell and say '<s>namo Buddhāya</s>' (homage to the Buddha)—their five heinous <s>karmas</s> shall be exhausted.

body.translated_text: Then the prince, having spoken the verses to his father, stood in silence. Then King <s>Ajitasena</s> spoke thus to his own son: 'How do you know, prince, that this monk has entered <s>samādhi</s>?' Then King <s>Ajitasena</s>, upon seeing the form, color, marks, and proportions of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, fainted and fell to the ground. children.text: ) ayamānanda nandimitramahāśrāvakastatraiva kālasamaye nandiprabho nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksambuddho loke bhaviṣyati / ānanda āha / kīdṛśaṃ bhagavan teṣāṃ tathāgatānāṃ buddhakṣetraṃ bhaviṣyati / bhagavānāha / aparimitaguṇasañcayā nāma sā buddhakṣetraṃ bhaviṣyati yatreme tathāgatā bhaviṣyanti / ānanda āha / ya imaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ sakalaṃ samāptaṃ paścime kāle paścime samaye samprakāśayiṣyati tasya kīdṛśaḥ puṇyaskandho bhaviṣyati / bhagavānāha / yadā mayānanda duṣkarakoṭiniyutaśatasahasrāṇi caritvā bodhirabhisambuddhā tadā te sattvā bodhimabhisambhotsyante / ya etaddharmaparyāyāt catuṣpadikāmapi gāthāṃ śroṣyanti avaivartikāśca te sattvā bhaviṣyantyanuttarāyāṃ samyaksambodhau / ānanda āha / ya imaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ dharmabhāṇakāḥ samprakāśayiṣyanti teṣāṃ kīdṛśaṃ kuśalamūlaṃ bhaviṣyati / bhagavānāha / śṛṇu ānanda rājā bhaviṣyati cakravartī caturdvīpeśvaraḥ / ya imaṃ dhamaparyāyaṃ sakalaṃ samāptaṃ samprakāśayiṣyanti muktāśca bhaviṣyanti jātijarāvyādhiparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsebhyaḥ parimuktā bhaviṣyanti / ānanda āha / ye paścime kāle paścime samaye sattvā imaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ pratikṣepsyanti na pattīyiṣyanti teṣāṃ kā gatirbhaviṣyati kaḥ parāyaṇam / (
children.translated_text: ) This <s>Nandimitra</s>, the great <s>śrāvaka</s>, O <s>Ānanda</s>, at the proper time in that very [realm], will become a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Nandiprabha</s> (Splendor of Joy), an <s>arhat</s>, a perfectly enlightened one, in the world. <s>Ānanda</s> asked: 'What will the <s>buddhakṣetra</s> (buddha-field) of those <s>Tathāgatas</s> be like, <s>Bhagavān</s>?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'That <s>buddhakṣetra</s>, where these <s>Tathāgatas</s> will arise, will be named <s>Aparimitaguṇasañcayā</s> (Accumulation of Limitless Qualities).' <s>Ānanda</s> asked: 'What will be the mass of merit for one who proclaims this <s>dharmaparyāya</s> (discourse on the Dharma) in its entirety in the last time, the last period?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'When I, <s>Ānanda</s>, having practiced through hundreds of thousands of millions of millions of difficult deeds, fully awakened to <s>bodhi</s> (awakening) — then those beings too will fully awaken to <s>bodhi</s>. Those who hear even a single four-line verse from this <s>dharmaparyāya</s> will become <s>avaivartika</s> (irreversible) in unsurpassed perfect awakening.' <s>Ānanda</s> asked: 'What will be the root of wholesome merit for those <s>dharmabhāṇakas</s> (preachers of the Dharma) who proclaim this <s>dharmaparyāya</s>?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Listen, <s>Ānanda</s> — he will become a <s>Cakravartin</s> (universal monarch), lord of the four continents. Those who proclaim this <s>dharmaparyāya</s> in its entirety will be liberated — liberated from birth, old age, disease, lamentation, suffering, mental anguish, and tribulation.' <s>Ānanda</s> asked: 'What destiny will those beings have who, in the last time, the last period, reject this <s>dharmaparyāya</s> and do not believe in it? What will be their final resort?'

children.translated_text: ) The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Enough, enough, <s>Ānanda</s>! Do not ask me about that evil mass of <s>karma</s>. I am unable to proclaim it fully — even hundreds of millions of <s>Buddhas</s> would be unable to proclaim it fully.' <s>Ānanda</s> said: 'Proclaim it, <s>Bhagavān</s>, proclaim it, <s>Sugata</s>!' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Listen, <s>Ānanda</s>, I shall proclaim the destiny of one who rejects the true <s>Dharma</s>. In the <s>Raurava</s> great hell, in the <s>Hāhaha</s> great hell, in the <s>Avīci</s> great hell, in the animal realm, in the world of <s>Yama</s>, and in the domain of <s>pretas</s> (hungry ghosts), suffering must be endured for many thousands of <s>kalpas</s> (aeons). If at some time one is reborn in the human world, one will have a long, dry palate and throat. One's tongue will extend twelve <s>yojanas</s> (leagues). Twelve ploughshares will pass over it. Those who have spoken such words [of rejection] — "Do not, O sons of good families, ever reject the true <s>Dharma</s>!" — such is the destiny of one who rejects the true <s>Dharma</s>.' <s>Ānanda</s> asked: 'For what reason, <s>Bhagavān</s>, is the true <s>Dharma</s> rejected?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Those beings who, in the last time, the last period, will revile, abuse, disparage, and slander these <s>sūtra</s>-holders and <s>dharmabhāṇakas</s> (preachers of the Dharma), who will generate a hostile mind toward those <s>dharmabhāṇakas</s> — by them the true <s>Dharma</s> will have been rejected. Just so, whoever looks with a hostile mind at these <s>sūtra</s>-holders and <s>dharmabhāṇakas</s> — this one will produce a mass of demerit greater than that.'

body.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> addressed the <s>Bhagavān</s> thus: 'This King <s>Ajitasena</s>, having renounced his kingdom, having built a monastery, has gone forth into the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s teaching. What root of merit will be his?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Excellent, excellent, <s>Ānanda</s>, that you have proclaimed this! This King <s>Ajitasena</s>, having gone forth in my teaching — in the future, after immeasurable, inconceivable, immeasurable <s>kalpas</s>, a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Ajitaprabha</s> (Unconquered Radiance) will arise in the world, an <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened, endowed with knowledge and conduct, <s>Sugata</s>, knower of the world, unsurpassed, tamer of those to be tamed, teacher of gods and men, <s>Buddha</s>, <s>Bhagavān</s>.' <s>Ānanda</s> said: 'This great <s>śrāvaka Nandimitra</s> was the king's spiritual friend. body.text: atha ānando bhagavato gāthāḥ pratyabhāṣata /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Ānanda</s> addressed the <s>Bhagavān</s> with verses:

children.text: bahusūtrasahasrāṇi śrutaṃ me śāstusammukhāt /
children.translated_text: 'Many thousands of <s>sūtras</s> have been heard by me in the Teacher's presence;

children.text: na came īdṛśaṃ sūtraṃ śrutapūrvaṃ kadācana //
children.translated_text: never before have I heard a <s>sūtra</s> like this one.

children.text: parinirvṛtasya śāstusya paścātkāle subhairave /
children.translated_text: After the <s>Parinirvāṇa</s> of the Teacher, in the last time, so terrible,

children.text: idaṃ sūtraṃ prakāśiṣye dhārayiṣye imaṃ nayam //
children.translated_text: I shall proclaim this <s>sūtra</s> and shall uphold this teaching.

children.text: yatra sūtraratne asmiṃ paścātkāle bhaviṣyati /
children.translated_text: Wherever this jewel of a <s>sūtra</s> will be in the future time,

children.text: rakṣāṃ kariṣyāmi teṣāṃ paścātkāle subhairave //
children.translated_text: I shall provide protection for those [who uphold it] in the last time, so terrible.

body.text: pratikṣipiṣyāmi nedaṃ gambhīraṃ buddhabhāṣitam //
body.translated_text: I shall not reject this profound <s>Buddha</s>-word.'

body.text: athāyuṣmānānando bhagavato gāthā bhāṣitvā tūṣṇīṃ sthito 'bhūt / atha kāśyapo mahāśrāvako bhagavantaṃ gāthābhiradhyabhāṣata /
body.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, having spoken these verses to the <s>Bhagavān</s>, stood in silence. Then <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the great <s>śrāvaka</s>, addressed the <s>Bhagavān</s> with verses:

this unsurpassed <s>sūtra</s> has been proclaimed — may it not [be lost] in the future time, when the <s>Jina</s> has attained <s>Parinirvāṇa</s>;

body.translated_text:
'Of golden hue, with limbs endowed with supreme marks, bearing the thirty-two marks, the <s>Jina</s> (Victor) —
this well-spoken <s>sūtra</s> of great power, with a profound <s>Dharma</s>, subtle and difficult to perceive —

children.text: dhāriṣye maṃ sūtranayaṃ niruttaraṃ /
children.translated_text: I shall uphold this unsurpassed <s>sūtra</s>-teaching.'

children.text: athāyuṣmān śāradvatīputro bhagavantaṃ gāthābhiradhyabhāṣata /
children.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s> (Śāriputra) addressed the <s>Bhagavān</s> with verses:

children.text: namo 'stu te buddha mahānubhāva prakāśitaṃ sutramidaṃ niruttaram /
children.translated_text: 'Homage to you, O <s>Buddha</s> of great power! This unsurpassed <s>sūtra</s> has been proclaimed.

children.text: parinirvṛtasya tava lokanāyakā likhiṣyati sūtrametaṃ niruttaram //
children.translated_text: After your <s>Parinirvāṇa</s>, O Leaders of the World, they shall copy this unsurpassed <s>sūtra</s>.

body.text: na cāpi so gacchati durgatībhayaṃ svargaṃ ca so gacchati kṣiprametat //
body.translated_text: And that one shall not go to the fear of bad destinies, but shall quickly go to heaven.'

body.text: athāyuṣmān pūrṇo maitrāyaṇīputro bhagavantaṃ gāthābhiradhyabhāṣata /
body.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Pūrṇa Maitrāyaṇīputra</s> addressed the <s>Bhagavān</s> with verses:

children.text: kṛtajño bahusattvānāṃ mocako durgatībhayāt /
children.translated_text: 'Grateful one, liberator of many beings from the fear of bad destinies —

children.text: prakāśitaṃ tvayā sūtraṃ gambhīraṃ buddhadakṣiṇam //
children.translated_text: this profound <s>sūtra</s>, a worthy offering to the <s>Buddhas</s>, has been proclaimed by you.

children.text: ahaṃ hi paścime kāle nirvṛte tvayi nāyake /
children.translated_text: In the last time, when you, the Leader, have attained <s>Nirvāṇa</s>,

children.text: idaṃ sūtraṃ prakāśiṣye hitāya sarvaprāṇinām //
children.translated_text: I shall proclaim this <s>sūtra</s> for the benefit of all living beings.'

body.text: iti /
body.translated_text: Thus.

body.translated_text: Then <s>Brahmā Sahāmpati</s> addressed the <s>Bhagavān</s> with verses:

body.translated_text: 'Homage to you, O <s>Buddha</s> of great power! This auspicious <s>sūtra</s> has been proclaimed by you.

body.text: atha catvāro mahārājā bhagavantaṃ gāthābhiradhyabhāṣanta /
body.translated_text: Then the Four Great Kings (<s>Caturmahārājas</s>) addressed the <s>Bhagavān</s> with verses:

children.text: aho suramyaṃ varasūtraratnaṃ prakāśitam īdṛśa paścakāle /
children.translated_text: 'Oh, how beautiful is this supreme jewel of a <s>sūtra</s>, proclaimed in this manner for the future time!

children.text: ..................sūtraratnaṃ prakāśitaṃ paśyati paścakāle //
children.translated_text: ...this jewel of a <s>sūtra</s> proclaimed — may [beings] see it in the future time!

children.text: sugatāna vai lokavināyakānāṃ ahaṃ hi dhāriṣyam sūtraratnam /
children.translated_text: Of the <s>Sugatas</s> (Well-Gone Ones), the leaders of the world — I shall uphold this jewel of a <s>sūtra</s>;

children.text: rakṣāṃ kariṣyāmyaha sūtraratnaṃ imavocadbhagavānāttamanā //
children.translated_text: I shall provide protection for this jewel of a <s>sūtra</s>.' Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān</s>, delighted.

body.text: sā ca sarvāvatī parṣadbhagavato bhāṣitamabhyanandat /
body.translated_text: And that entire assembly rejoiced at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s words.

body.text: ajitasenavyakaraṇanirdeśo nāma mahāyānasūtraṃ samāptam //
body.translated_text: The <s>Mahāyāna sūtra</s> called the <s>Ajitasenavyākaraṇanirdeśa</s> (Exposition of the Prophecy of <s>Ajitasena</s>) is concluded.

deyadharmoyaṃ bālosiṃhena sārdha bhāryājājatitrana sārdhaṃ mātāpitroḥ paramaduṣkartroḥ sārdhaṃ kṣīṇīena akhiloṭiena diśoṭajāja maṅgali.......
utrayannagarvidoṭiena vaṭrari-khuśoṭi-khūśogoṭiena sārdhaṃ sarvasattvaiḥ sarva...... bhiryatra puṇya tadbha......
sarvasattvānāmanuttaraḥ...... sārdhaṃ paramakalyāṇamitrasthirabandhuena / lisvitamidaṃ pustakaṃ dharmabhāṇakanarendradattena /
body.translated_text: This is the meritorious gift of <s>Bālosiṃha</s>, together with [his] wife <s>Jājatitrana</s>, together with [his] parents of exceedingly difficult [acquisition of merit], together with <s>Kṣīṇī</s>, <s>Akhiloṭi</s>, <s>Diśoṭajāja</s>, <s>Maṅgali</s>... <s>Utrayannagarvidoṭi</s>, <s>Vaṭrari-khuśoṭi-khūśogoṭi</s>, together with all beings, all... wherever merit, may that be... for the unsurpassed [awakening] of all beings... together with the supreme spiritual friend <s>Sthirabandhu</s>. This manuscript was written by the <s>dharmabhāṇaka</s> (preacher of the Dharma) <s>Narendradatta</s>.
